subject: CAIQ adjudication: runtime feature-flagging & canary logs
messages:
From: Paul Bennett <paul.bennett@compliancepartners.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ follow-up — runtime controls (feature flags & canary logs)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move into the CAIQ control mapping for EdgeWave Security, two items came up from their auditor that we'd like to adjudicate with Redwood:

- CCM_GRC-1 (Change Management / Runtime): auditor wants evidence that runtime feature flags are governed (who can flip, audit trail, rollback controls).
- CCM_OBSV-4 (Operational Monitoring / Canarying): they requested a sample of canary logs and the retention/segregation approach used for canary telemetry.

Could you provide a quick mapping (control -> Redwood artifact) and a representative log sample for the canary behavior? A short playbook of how we extract the sample would also help.

If possible, we need the materials by EOD Thursday so the audit team can review before Friday's closure call.

Thanks — I can take a first pass and annotate on your matrix.

Paul Bennett
Compliance Partners LLC
paul.bennett@compliancepartners.io
+1 415-555-0108

Attachments: none
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Paul Bennett <paul.bennett@compliancepartners.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up — runtime controls (feature flags & canary logs)

Paul — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (controls owner for runtime change procedures) and David (observability / canary owner).

Quick plan:
1) Kimberly will attach a mapping document (control -> artifact) that points to policy excerpts, RBAC roles, and the audit event types we surface.
2) David will pull a redacted canary log tarball (PII-free) and a short extraction playbook.
3) I'll review and add an assertion narrative for the CAIQ entry.

Kimberly / David — can you target an initial package (matrix + 1 sample log tar) by Thu 18:00 PT? I added the auditor's control codes above to keep the mapping specific.

Sofia
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: none
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Paul Bennett <paul.bennett@compliancepartners.io>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up — runtime controls (feature flags & canary logs)

Thanks Sofia. Paul — attaching the first draft mapping: caiq_runtime_featureflag_mapping_v1.xlsx (columns: CAIQ control, Redwood assertion, artifact path, owner, sample ids). Highlights:

- For CCM_GRC-1 (Change Management / Runtime):
  * Assertion: Runtime feature flags are managed through our internal FlagService with enforced RBAC (role: release-engineer, SRE), approval workflow in Confluence + JIRA deployment gate, and immutable audit events written to our event store (events: flag.toggle.request, flag.toggle.approve, flag.toggle.execute).
  * Artifacts: excerpt of FlagService ACLs (artifact id: ACL-FF-2026-03), Confluence approval template (APPROVAL-TPL-FF), and a sample audit event export (audit_events_ff_sample.json).

- For CCM_OBSV-4 (Operational Monitoring / Canarying):
  * Assertion: Canary releases are instrumented via CanaryRunner; telemetry is routed to a dedicated telemetry namespace and retained for 90 days. Canary toggles and ramp percentages are recorded in the same audit stream as flags.
  * Artifacts: canary runbook excerpt (CANARY-RB-2.1), retention policy excerpt (retention-policy.yaml), and the canary log tar we plan to attach.

I've flagged two items for David to confirm: the canonical path to the audit export and whether the sample needs additional redaction.

Attached: caiq_runtime_featureflag_mapping_v1.xlsx

Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: caiq_runtime_featureflag_mapping_v1.xlsx
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Paul Bennett <paul.bennett@compliancepartners.io>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up — runtime controls (feature flags & canary logs)

Kimberly / Sofia / Paul — quick note on the log package and extraction steps.

I pulled a representative canary run segment from our CanaryRunner namespace (redacted for customer identifiers). Files included in the tar: canary-run-20260818/metrics.log, canary-run-20260818/trace.json, canary-run-20260818/manifest.yaml. Sample tar: canary_logs_sample_20260818.tar.gz (attached).

Extraction/playbook (playbook_runtime-ff-extract.txt):
- Step 1: snapshot CanaryRunner namespace for window 2026-08-18T02:00Z -> 2026-08-18T04:00Z.
- Step 2: run ff_log_exporter --namespace canary-runner --window start,end --redact customer_id,email --output tar.gz.
- Step 3: validate redaction via quick grep for email patterns and remove artifacts if any found.
- Step 4: upload tarball to secured Drive folder and add link to HubSpot evidence record.

Retention note: the telemetry namespace enforces 90-day retention by lifecycle policy; older artifacts are garbage-collected monthly. Audit events for flag actions are retained for 365 days in the event store (exportable on request).

Let me know if you need the raw export (longer retention/keys) — we'd need a DPA addendum for that.

David Kim
Observability Engineering
Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

Attachments: canary_logs_sample_20260818.tar.gz; playbook_runtime-ff-extract.txt
From: Paul Bennett <paul.bennett@compliancepartners.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up — runtime controls (feature flags & canary logs)

Thanks everyone — this is exactly what we needed. I reviewed the mapping and the sample tar; redaction looks good. A couple of quick follow-ups from the auditor:

- Can you add the event store export path and a short note on the HSM-based signing used for audit event immutability? (Kimberly / Sofia)
- Please include a signed attestation (one paragraph) that the canary sample is production-observed telemetry and that no customer PII is included. We can accept that as a self-attestation and reference it in the CAIQ narrative.

If you can drop the attestation as a short email reply and add the event-store path into the mapping sheet, we can close the EdgeWave package and move to the DocuSign step for the CAIQ acceptance. HubSpot ID is in the related links for reference.

Paul
Compliance Partners LLC
